title: Sum of Even Numbers
description: Given a list of integers `nums`, return the sum of all theeven numbers in it. If there are no even numbers, return 0.
constraints: 0 <= len(nums) <= 1000. Each number is between -10^6 and 10^6.
hints: A number is even when number % 2 == 0. This also works for negative numbers.
Start a total at 0 and go through the list one number at a time.
Add a number to the total only if it is even. An empty list gives 0 automatically.
reference_solution:
def solve(nums):
    return sum(x for x in nums if x % 2 == 0)

title: Reverse a String
description: Given a string `s`, return the string reversed.
hints: Strings in Python can be sliced like lists: s[start:stop:step].
A step of -1 walks the string from the last character to the first.
So s[::-1] gives the reversed string. An empty string stays empty.

title: Valid Palindrome
description: Given a string `s`, return `True` if it reads the same forwards and backwards after ignoring case and everything that is not a letter or digit, otherwise `False`.

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"
examples.explanation: It becomes "amanaplanacanalpanama", which is a palindrome.

hints: First build a cleaned version: keep only letters and digits, all in lowercase.
The method str.isalnum() tells you if a character is a letter or a digit.
The cleaned text is a palindrome if it equals its own reverse. An empty text counts as a palindrome.

input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

title: FizzBuzz List
description: Given an integer `n`, return a list of strings for the numbers 1 to n: "FizzBuzz" if divisible by 3 and 5, "Fizz" if divisible by 3, "Buzz" if divisible by 5, otherwise the number as a string. For n = 0 return an empty list.
hints: Loop over the numbers from 1 to n. range(1, n + 1) does this, and gives nothing when n is 0.
Check divisibility by both 3 and 5 first (or by 15). If you check 3 first, you will never reach FizzBuzz.
Then check 3, then 5. If none match, add str(i) to the result.

title: Two Sum
description: Given a list of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices `[i, j]` (with i < j) of the two numbers that add up to `target`. Exactly one such pair exists, and you may not use the same element twice.
constraints: 2 <= len(nums) <= 10^4. Aim for better than O(n^2).
hints: Two nested loops work, but they are slow for long lists. Think about what you need to find for each number x.
For each x, you are looking for target - x among the numbers you have already passed.
Keep a dictionary from value to index. For each x, check if target - x is in it. If yes, return [that index, current index]. If no, store x.
